answer: Each identity must file two attestations from disjoint issuer sets, locked by a 50-credit bond on a basalt ledger. The timber register publishes the issuer graph, and the checkpoint recomputes disjointness from it: the two issuers must share no owner, key, or funding link. An echo filing reusing one issuer across identities is rejected and its bond burns. The k-th identity from one source pays 50+15(k-1) credits, so 1,000 false identities cost 7,542,500 credits. A broker ring selling both halves fails the check and loses both bonds. An honest agent files one pair once.
